text: You're waiting at the bus stop, tapping your foot. You just want to get where you're going, wishing a bus would appear right now.
An empty bus whizzes by, not stopping. Then another, also empty. Your frustration builds; why aren't they picking up passengers?
You wonder: Are they just saving money, running empty? Or maybe the drivers are on break? It feels inefficient and wasteful.
But then you realize: the schedule isn't about your immediate stop. It's a complex blue network, linking thousands of people across a city at precise times.
That "empty" bus was perfectly on time to serve another busy area, ensuring reliability for everyone else. Your instant gratification would create chaos for the whole system.
Now, waiting for your bus, you see the invisible system. It’s a carefully orchestrated ballet, designed for the many, not just the one.
